transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Hi, doctor. I can’t seem to slow down—I’m constantly taking on new projects and working nonstop, like I’m stuck in overdrive. It has just gotten to the point where I can't seem to turn it off.

Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt very down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day? If so, did that happen before this current high-energy period?

No, I can't say I've ever had a period of feeling down or losing interest in things like that. My main issue has actually been the exact opposite—I just can't seem to slow down and I'm constantly in overdrive.

Before this current high-energy period, have you ever had any separate episode in your life where you felt depressed or lost interest in most things for at least two weeks? Even if it was a long time ago, did anything like that ever happen?

No, I've never had any period in my life where I felt depressed or lost interest in things like that. Before this, my life was pretty normal and busy, so this current overdrive state is the only thing that has felt completely different and problematic for me.

During this high-energy period, have you had any experiences like hearing or seeing things others don’t, or strongly believing something that others said wasn’t true? Have you felt unusually suspicious or convinced you had special powers or abilities?

No, I don't hear or see things that aren't there, and I'm not suspicious of anyone. But I do feel like I'm destined to revolutionize how people use solar and smart homes because I can see brilliant solutions other electricians just aren't smart enough to understand.

Do other people tell you these ideas are unrealistic or impossible, and if so, are you still completely certain they’re true? Also, have you done anything risky or out of character because of these beliefs, like spending a lot of money or making major life decisions?

My wife and boss keep telling me my plans are unrealistic and that I need to slow down, but I'm 100% certain they're wrong and they'll thank me later. To get the business moving, I did order a lot of expensive tools and solar inventory on credit, which has run up some major debt and made my wife absolutely furious. I still feel it was a completely necessary step for what I'm building, though.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a distinct current episode of persistently elevated/overactive energy with nonstop projects, grandiose beliefs held with delusional conviction despite clear contradiction from wife and boss, and risky excessive spending causing major debt and interpersonal conflict. There is no history of prior depressive episodes elicited in the interview. Psychotic features are mood-congruent grandiose delusional beliefs occurring in the context of a manic syndrome, supporting manic episode with psychotic symptoms.
